response.text:
Training-prefix sensitivity establishes that a fitted model reacts to its inputs; it cannot alone distinguish memorized prefix–target associations from generalizable sequence use. Shuffling studies find weak sequential structure in several popular recommendation datasets, and order effects can reflect item availability as well as user behavior. Thus, a performance drop after shuffling is evidence of order sensitivity, not proof of learned behavioral dynamics. [Dataset analysis](https://publications.hse.ru/en/chapters/984043670), [user-pattern versus item-availability analysis](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042).

Recommended diagnostic protocol: freeze the trained HSTU checkpoint and compare original versus perturbed histories on the existing validation users, retaining identical targets, candidate sets, filtering and seeds. Shuffle only nonpadding positions; separately shuffle older history while preserving the final item, truncate older context, and remove the final item. Preserve left padding and read the final nonpadding position. Report paired HR@10 changes, target-rank changes and user-bootstrap uncertainty for each category, plus the pinned macro average. Repeat perturbations to estimate diagnostic variability; these are input interventions on one model, not prediction ensembles. Keep training-prefix results explicitly separate as in-sample diagnostics.

Interpretation: reproducible validation degradation when older order changes but item membership and the final item remain fixed supports generalizable order dependence within this benchmark. Sensitivity concentrated on training prefixes is consistent with memorization or distribution shift, but does not establish either. Stratify validation effects by training-observed transition frequency and suffix overlap without changing splits; persistence on novel transitions strengthens the evidence. Availability artifacts remain an alternative explanation, and fixed-split diagnostics cannot establish validity under a different temporal evaluation protocol. [Evaluation limitations](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748164).
